## Task 1

**a) Why does an arrival event need to generate a new arrival event?**

The simulator only knows about future events through the event list. When an arrival event is executed, it must schedule the next arrival. Otherwise, only the first customer would ever arrive: once the events already on the list were processed, the list would be empty and the simulation would stop. Each arrival therefore schedules the next one, which keeps the stream of customers coming for the whole run.

**b) Which event should be generated by the start of the service(of single service point)?**

The start of a service (a C-event) should schedule the corresponding end-of-service event, i.e. a B-event that marks the completion of that activity. The service time is known when the service starts, so the finish is scheduled at clock + service duration. For example, C2 (operator 1 starts) schedules B4 at clock + 4, and C3 (operator 2 starts) schedules B5 at clock + 7.
